en.headline: Meta says it met Hong Kong privacy watchdog over AI glasses concerns
en.dek: The company briefed media after the Privacy Commissioner warned that smart glasses could enable covert recording and excessive data collection processed by AI.
body: Meta Platforms confirmed on Monday that it had discussed privacy concerns surrounding its AI-enabled smart glasses with Hong Kong's Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data.

The meeting followed the PCPD's issuance last week of guidance warning that the glasses could enable covert recording, excessive collection of personal data, and processing of sensitive information through AI systems.

Philip Chua, Meta's public policy director for products in Asia-Pacific, said the company takes the office's counsel and continues to work with them to address concerns as the products go on sale in the city.

zh.headline: Meta稱已就AI眼鏡私隱憂慮與私隱公署會面
zh.dek: 公司在私隱專員警告智能眼鏡可能導致隱蔽攝錄及AI處理過量資料後，向傳媒簡報。
body: Meta平台周一確認，已就其AI智能眼鏡的私隱問題，與香港個人資料私隱專員公署進行討論。
是次會面是在公署上周發布指引後進行，指引警告該眼鏡可能促成隱蔽攝錄、過度收集個人資料，以及透過AI系統處理敏感資訊。
Meta亞太區產品公共政策總監蔡偉麟表示，公司會採納公署意見，並繼續與對方合作，以解決相關憂慮，同時產品在本港發售。
